title: When the Postcard Burns
premise: Yara Nystrom has built a career on other people's words, ghostwriting the memoir of her rival, bestselling author Elias Vane, while hiding a decade-long secret: anonymous letters she wrote to a stranger named 'D,' the only place she ever told the truth. When a quiet new neighbor, Daniel Okoye, moves in next door, Yara recognizes his handwriting and realizes 'D' has spent ten years falling for a woman who doesn't exist. As Elias's memoir threatens to expose the letters—and a buried injustice from their shared past that Daniel has spent years investigating—Yara must choose between protecting her invisibility and claiming her name. In the end, she burns the postcards, testifies to the truth Elias tried to bury, and writes her first book under her own signature, giving Daniel not the letters, but herself.
about_author: M. M. Okonkwo is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's correspondence before writing fiction of her own. She lives between Lagos and Copenhagen and believes every unsent letter is a novel waiting to happen.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Contract
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She signs a lucrative contract to ghostwrite rival author Elias Vane's memoir, hiding her resentment behind professional detachment. Establishes her rule: lend pieces of the heart, never the whole. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness disguised as ambition.

chapters.title: Return to Sender
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Packing her late mother's house, Yara rereads the bundle of replies from 'D'—ten years of letters to an anonymous pen pal she found through a bookstore's dead-letter box. She almost burns them, but can't. Emotional beat: tender ache for the one honest relationship she's ever had.

chapters.title: The Man Next Door
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A moving truck arrives next door; Daniel Okoye helps her carry a box up icy stairs. Something in his handwriting on a package label stops her cold. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past arriving in the present tense.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel unpacks, revealing to the reader he has known for months that his new neighbor is his anonymous correspondent. He's spent a decade writing to 'Y' while investigating a wrongful conviction tied to a publishing scandal. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into patience.

chapters.title: Borrowed Voices
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Interviewing Elias for his memoir, she hears him describe a plagiarism scandal he survived by letting his editor take the fall—a man named Okoye. Yara realizes Daniel's father was destroyed to protect Elias's career. Emotional beat: dread blooming under professional composure.

chapters.title: Coffee, Carefully Measured
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel courts Yara in small domestic gestures—coffee over the fence, borrowed tools—testing whether the woman matches the letters. She is funnier and more frightened than her words. Emotional beat: falling for the real person, not the myth.

chapters.title: What the Letters Never Said
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Elias's memoir deadline looms; he wants a chapter on 'the scandal that made me.' Yara stalls, digging through archives for what really happened to Daniel's father. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Handwriting on the Wall
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel nearly reveals himself when he quotes a line from her letters aloud; Yara deflects, terrified that the fantasy will collapse into an ordinary, disappointing man—or worse, that she'll disappoint him. Emotional beat: the cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: Elias Wants a Villain
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Elias, sensing Yara knows something, threatens to expose her ghostwriting career if she undermines his memoir's narrative. He shows her a postcard he intercepted years ago—one of her letters to 'D.' Emotional beat: blackmail tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Archive
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, intercut with a letter flashback. Yara breaks into the publishing house's archive and finds proof Elias plagiarized Daniel's father's manuscript. She photographs everything, hands shaking. Emotional beat: the ghostwriter finally stealing words back for their true owner.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Knew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara confronts Daniel: how long has he known who she is? He admits he recognized her handwriting the day he moved in. Betrayal and relief collide—she was seen all along. Emotional beat: rage at being loved under false pretenses, then realizing she did the same.

chapters.title: Past Tense
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel tells her why he never said anything: every time he tried, he feared losing the only honest thing in his life, and he needed her to choose him freely. She walks out. Emotional beat: love offered too late to feel safe.

chapters.title: The Memoir Draft
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Elias's ghostwritten chapters are due; he demands she write his innocence into history. Yara submits a draft that quietly tells the truth instead, burying the evidence in plain sight. Emotional beat: quiet rebellion dressed as obedience.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Elias discovers the draft's double meaning and gives her forty-eight hours to rewrite it or he releases her letters publicly, destroying her anonymity and Daniel's case. She goes home and holds a postcard over the stove. Emotional beat: the temptation to erase herself one last time.

chapters.title: What D Never Knew
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Yara's POV through the letters themselves. The origin story: why she started writing to a stranger after her mother's disgrace, and why she invented a version of herself brave enough to tell the truth. Emotional beat: compassion for her own younger self.

chapters.title: The Case Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel's father, dying, asks him to drop the fight and keep his name clean. Daniel must decide whether justice is worth the wreckage. Yara arrives with the archive photos. Emotional beat: grief and resolve fusing into a plan.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara and Daniel race to authenticate the manuscript and secure a journalist before Elias's deadline. Elias counters by leaking one letter early, exposing Yara's ghostwriting to the industry. Emotional beat: everything she built burning down to the studs.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At a public literary event, instead of Elias's sanitized memoir excerpt, Yara reads aloud the true story of Daniel Okoye's father, naming Elias on stage. Chaos, cameras, her career detonating in real time. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into freedom.

chapters.title: Ashes and Evidence
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. In the fallout, Elias's publisher opens an investigation; Daniel's father's manuscript is authenticated. Elias, cornered, offers Yara hush money and a byline. She refuses and finally burns the postcards—not to forget, but to stop hiding in them. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: First Person, Present Tense
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Months later: Yara's own book, written under her name, is going to press. Daniel asks what she'll do now that she's visible to everyone. Emotional beat: learning to be loved without a mask.

chapters.title: When the Postcard Burns
chapters.summary: Yara and Daniel's POVs alternating. On the anniversary of their first letter, they meet at the bookstore's dead-letter box and exchange one final, signed letter each—no anonymity, no past tense. Emotional beat: the whole heart, risked and received.

chapters.title: Signed, Yara
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue. At her first public reading, she dedicates the book to 'the stranger who answered,' and Daniel stands up in the third row. Her father's-name-clearing victory and her own name on the cover close the circle. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging.
